We further study whether an adversary can actively engineer prompts that amplify this effect, using the model as a covert carrier to transmit secrets through seemingly innocuous text. In both cases, this limited leakage is exploited using a novel adaptive attack that assumes black-box access to the underlying model. In controlled experiments across eight proprietary models, we find that 2-digit in-context secrets are reconstructed with near-perfect accuracy and 4-digit secrets at 82\% exact match, all from outputs the model produces in response to ordinary, non-adversarial requests. We observe that more capable models leak more: stronger instruction-following amplifies sensitivity to in-context secrets, suggesting leakage is a byproduct of capability as opposed to a patchable bug. We show this leakage enables two practical attacks: (1) a trained classifier that infers semantic predicates about user memories (e.g., health conditions, financial events) from routine natural-language outputs, and (2) an RL-trained adversary that extracts full Social Security Numbers from a production-style agent. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Predicting Dose-Response Success from Primary Screening Data
docs.text:
Predicting Dose-Response Success from Primary Screening Data Predicting Dose-Response Success from Primary Screening Data arXiv:2608.26538v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: High-throughput drug screening uses inexpensive primary screens to select compounds for more costly follow-up dose-response experiments, which estimate compound potency (pXC50) by determining the concentration required to produce a specified biological effect. However, many promoted compounds fail to yield a reportable potency, even when activity is subsequently confirmed. We investigated whether inexpensive three-point primary-screening data could predict whether a more costly 11-point dose-response experiment would yield a reportable pXC50. Using a dataset of 32,971 compound-assay pairs with three-point primary-screening and 11-point dose-response measurements, we trained random-forest models to predict successful potency quantification. Our model achieved an AUROC of 0.939 +/- 0.002 and generalized to previously unseen chemical scaffolds and assay-mechanism families. We found that primary-screen response features were more predictive of dose-response quantifiability than molecular structure-based features. Successful potency quantification was also strongly associated with primary-screen response amplitude. Across eight chronological test releases, the model retrospectively retained 90% of reportable potencies while selecting only 55.7% of historically promoted compound-assay pairs for follow-up profiling. These findings suggest that predicting potency quantifiability from primary-screening data could improve the efficiency of compound prioritization and reduce unnecessary dose-response experiments. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Simulation-free Unbalanced Dynamic Optimal Transport with General Growth Penalty
docs.text:
Simulation-free Unbalanced Dynamic Optimal Transport with General Growth Penalty Simulation-free Unbalanced Dynamic Optimal Transport with General Growth Penalty arXiv:2609.04710v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Inferring cellular dynamics from unpaired single-cell snapshots requires modeling both state transitions and population growth or death. Unbalanced dynamic optimal transport (UDOT) addresses this by penalizing growth along transport paths, making the choice of growth penalty a key way to encode biological priors on proliferation and apoptosis. However, existing UDOT solvers either rely on computationally expensive NeuralODE simulations or depend on analytical solutions of conditional paths, restricting their efficiency solely to quadratic penalties, i.e. Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geodesics. To enable an efficient UDOT solver for general growth penalties, we first show that concave growth penalties lead to degenerate solutions where growth and transport are separated. We then introduce \textbf{S}imulation-free \textbf{U}nbalanced \textbf{D}ynamic \textbf{O}ptimal transport (SUDO), a simulation-free framework for UDOT with general non-quadratic convex growth penalties. SUDO learns the conditional paths and transport costs, solves the induced semi-coupling problem, and subsequently leverages unbalanced flow matching to achieve a simulation-free solution. On WFR benchmarks, SUDO matches the accuracy of efficient, analytical solution-driven algorithms while outperforming simulation-based methods in computational speed. Beyond WFR, SUDO supports asymmetric penalties that encode proliferation-dominant priors and produce more plausible trajectories and growth estimates on synthetic and single-cell datasets. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: HyCO: A Hybrid Neural Solver for Combinatorial Optimization
docs.text:
HyCO: A Hybrid Neural Solver for Combinatorial Optimization HyCO: A Hybrid Neural Solver for Combinatorial Optimization arXiv:2609.07990v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Sequential reinforcement learning (RL) solvers and global diffusion model (DM) solvers for neural combinatorial optimization exhibit complementary failure modes under an optimization-regret view. The former enjoys small marginal regret in the early construction stage, but suffers from horizon-wise compounding errors with super-linear regret growth; the latter avoids horizon compounding but incurs linear or sublinear regret w.r.t. the dimension of the remaining unsolved subspace. We propose Hybrid Neural Solver for Combinatorial Optimization (HyCO), a hybrid inference algorithm that constructs a solution prefix with an RL solver and adaptively switches to a conditional DM to complete the remaining decisions. To characterize why such hybridization helps, when to trigger the handover, and how to realize it in practice, we first develop a unified error-scaling theoretical framework and prove that, under explicit error-scaling assumptions, i) the hybrid structure achieves strictly lower expected regret than either backbone alone, and ii) there exists a unique optimal trigger step that minimizes the hybrid regret. We then design a lightweight adaptive trigger that combines policy entropy and RL-DM disagreement to detect trajectory-level signals of the regime shift as a practical proxy, since the optimal trigger step is defined at the expected-regret level and is not directly computable on individual trajectories. Experimental results on diverse benchmarks demonstrate that HyCO achieves consistent improvements over both backbones and support the empirical effectiveness of adaptive triggering. Our code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/wmd3i/HyCO. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Toward Optimal Switching Regret for Multi-Armed Bandits with Oblivious Adversary
docs.text:
Toward Optimal Switching Regret for Multi-Armed Bandits with Oblivious Adversary Toward Optimal Switching Regret for Multi-Armed Bandits with Oblivious Adversary arXiv:2609.13547v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study switching regret in adversarial multi-armed bandits, where the learner competes with an arm sequence that changes at most $S$ times. When $S$ is known, an optimal expected regret of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{(S+1)KT})$ is obtainable [Auer et al., 2002]. However, when $S$ is unknown, Marinov and Zimmert [2021] show that this guarantee is impossible under an adaptive adversary. In this paper, we show that a single algorithm achieves $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{(S+1)KT})$ expected regret for every $S$ against an oblivious adversary, resolving an open problem of Auer et al. [2019b]. Our algorithm combines a fixed-share learner initialized with a small learning rate and dyadic-interval subroutines that search for local improvements using randomized learning rates and implicit exploration. Importantly, a non-uniform prior favors following the main learner, keeping the cost of maintaining many subroutines small. When the subroutines accumulate sufficient improvement over the main learner, its learning rate doubles, allowing adaptation to the unknown number of comparator switches $S$. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: A Comprehensive View of Fairness through Distributional Stability
docs.text:
A Comprehensive View of Fairness through Distributional Stability A Comprehensive View of Fairness through Distributional Stability arXiv:2609.37061v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We view fairness as a property of distributional stability. Rather than assessing a predictor under a fixed data distribution, we study how its predictions change under perturbations that modify the composition of protected groups. A predictor is fair if it remains stable under such shifts. Under this perspective, several classical notions of fairness arise as stability with respect to specific perturbations, with the associated unfairness gap given by a Lipschitz constant of a prediction-rate functional. This formulation also yields guarantees that hold uniformly over a range of demographic compositions at test time, without requiring knowledge of the deployment distribution. It leads to a learning procedure based on convex combinations of reweighted predictors, formulated as a second-order cone program, for which we establish generalization bounds. Experiments on standard benchmarks illustrate the approach. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Non-Commutative Lie-Algebraic State-Space Models: Finite-Division Variety Laws, Semidirect Cascades, and Gradient Saddle Escape
docs.text:
Non-Commutative Lie-Algebraic State-Space Models: Finite-Division Variety Laws, Semidirect Cascades, and Gradient Saddle Escape Non-Commutative Lie-Algebraic State-Space Models: Finite-Division Variety Laws, Semidirect Cascades, and Gradient Saddle Escape arXiv:2610.00329v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Structured state-space sequence models (SSMs) achieve linear-time inference and logarithmic-time parallel training via associative scans, yet diagonal transitions generate solvable semigroups unable to track non-solvable group words or 3D rigid-body manifolds. We present Non-Commutative Lie-Algebraic State-Space Models (Lie-SSMs), parameterizing recurrent updates on Lie algebra tangent spaces via the matrix exponential. First, using an o-minimal cylindrical flag collar, we establish an unconditional single-layer finite-division criterion for contracting $SO(3)$ and $SU(2)$ heads, proving odd-prime Sylow abelianity, odd-$p$-core centrality, and exponent-30 commutator obstructions excluding $S_5$ in $SO(3)^m, SU(2)^m,$ and $SO(4)^m$ while identifying the sharp threshold $d^*(S_5)=d^*(A_6)=5$ in $SO(5)$. Second, Depth-2 semidirect and Schreier $2$-cocycle cascades resolve $S_5$, $2I\cong SL_2(F_5)$, and $\mathrm{Heis}(F_p)$ in $O(\log T)$ scan depth, whereas unnormalized contracting coupling collapses exponentially without Directional RMSNorm. Third, we characterize the $\Theta(\varepsilon^{c-1})$ Chen--Magnus--Hall--Witt commutator saddle and $1/|[G,G]|$ coset-centroid dilution, proving generic first-order symmetry breaking at $\varepsilon=0$ and teacher-forced local Polyak--\L{}ojasiewicz convergence under dense prefix supervision and factored readouts ($99.90\%/99.40\%$ on $S_5$ at $T=128$; $100.00\%$ on $D_{16}$). Across $SE_2(3)$ Left-Jacobian odometry, Hillis--Steele/Blelloch GPU scans ($48.24\times$ forward, $20.27\times/10.28\times$ full-layer speedup at $T=2048$), and three 3D IMU benchmarks (UCI HAR, UCI HAPT-PT, and 17-subject REALDISP), Lie-$SO(3)$ models reach $95.69\%\pm 0.14\%$ on HAR, $88.44\%\pm 0.83\%$ episode logit-vote ($83.97\%\pm 1.20\%$ C3 window in 30-subject 5-fold CV; $87.16\%\pm 0.64\%$ 9-subject split) on HAPT-PT, and $84.23\%\pm 1.00\%$ on REALDISP. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: SkillEvoLean: Mutation-enhanced skill evolution for Lean provers
docs.text:
SkillEvoLean: Mutation-enhanced skill evolution for Lean provers SkillEvoLean: Mutation-enhanced skill evolution for Lean provers arXiv:2610.01799v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Skill evolution offers a promising way to improve large language model agents without updating their parameters, but its use in formal theorem proving remains underexplored. Existing methods mainly target natural-language reasoning, improving skills by analyzing successful and failed trajectories and incrementally revising solving strategies. Although the Lean verifier provides reliable execution feedback, when all sampled trajectories fail, existing skill evolution methods lack successful trajectories from which to infer effective update directions. Furthermore, these methods also focus mainly on the root instruction file, thus underexploring the evolution of reference knowledge including mathematical concepts and proving techniques. To address these limitations, we propose a mutation-enhanced skill self-evolution framework for building skill-augmented Lean provers. The framework jointly evolves a high-level solving policy and its reference knowledge through progressive and mutation-based updates. Progressive evolution derives local improvements from successful and failed trajectories, while mutation is triggered when no complete proof can be generated, sampling mathematical concepts to produce and select new skill candidates under verifier feedback. We evaluate our method on MiniF2F, PutnamBench, the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO 2025), and the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad (USAMO 2026). Under the same backbone model, trajectorysampling budget, and test-time compute, our method achieves proof success rates of 100.0%, 90.6%, 4/6, and 4/6, respectively, with GPT-5.5, outperforming the baseline methods. Further analysis shows that concept-guided mutation outperforms random-text-guided mutation by 6.9 and 8.2 percentage points on MiniF2F and PutnamBench, respectively, while solving one additional problem on both IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Sharp Non-Asymptotic Analysis of the Penalized Challenger in $\beta$-EB-TCI for Bernoulli Bandits
docs.text:
Sharp Non-Asymptotic Analysis of the Penalized Challenger in $\beta$-EB-TCI for Bernoulli Bandits Sharp Non-Asymptotic Analysis of the Penalized Challenger in $\beta$-EB-TCI for Bernoulli Bandits arXiv:2610.01951v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Top-two algorithms are simple and effective for fixed-confidence best-arm identification, but their sharp non-asymptotic behavior is still not well understood. We study this question for Bernoulli bandits through $\beta$-EB-TCI, the empirical-best top-two rule of Jourdan et al., whose challenger minimizes a Bernoulli transportation cost plus a logarithmic penalty in its pull count. We first analyze the stabilized regime, in which the empirical leader has become the true best arm and its sampling fraction stays close to $\beta$. In this regime, every suboptimal arm is sampled linearly often, and, with high probability, the stopping time is at most $T_{\beta}^{\star}(\mu)\log(1/\delta)$ plus stabilization and lower-order concentration terms, with the exact fixed-$\beta$ leading coefficient. The main remaining difficulty is therefore to control when the regime is reached. For the original rule, we obtain a non-asymptotic high-probability stopping bound on every Bernoulli instance with a unique best arm. Under a finite-mean sufficient-exploration condition, the bound yields the sharp expected sample complexity; combined with the exploration result of Jourdan et al., this covers pairwise-distinct means under their tie-breaking convention. A mild forced-exploration guard, which uses only $O(\sqrt{Kt})$ pulls up to time $t$, gives a self-contained sharp expected bound for any number of arms with a unique best arm. We also identify a limitation of proof strategies that try to handle equal suboptimal means through a single index-comparison argument. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: What Does a Harness Repair? Three Preregistered Studies Around a Longevity-Tuned Language Model
docs.text:
What Does a Harness Repair? Three Preregistered Studies Around a Longevity-Tuned Language Model What Does a Harness Repair? Three Preregistered Studies Around a Longevity-Tuned Language Model arXiv:2610.05533v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: A harness search around a frozen longevity-tuned 1.7B model reported a rescue. An audit found that the gain came from rows the start left unparsed, that the caller sent each row's reference answer as an assistant turn, and that replication through the same pipeline missed it. Is a harness's gain more than a constant answer would give? We preregistered three studies and report every endpoint. In the first two, thinking off raised test accuracy over a capped thinking setting in 7 of 12 cells, mostly on rows the cap left unparsed. It was not meaningfully worse than a rescue in 7 of 9 small-model test cells or than four GEPA harnesses at 1.7B. Replication reproduced an injected defect's distortion in 9 of 20 evaluable cases (7 fixed by design). At 14B, two GEPA harnesses beat thinking off by 34 points on test but were not detectably above the strongest constant label, and answered "Yes" in 94.6% and 98.2% of parsed mortality answers on test. In the third study (SmolLM3-3B, base Qwen3-1.7B), GEPA beat the constant on FPB (confirmatory, both partitions); thinking off was not meaningfully worse than any BoolQ harness, and 3 of 4 MMLU-Pro searches kept their seed (the fourth inconclusive on test). On Autocast (exploratory), the harnesses were within 0.7 points of the constant and gave one label in 93.1% to 96.8% of parsed answers, both on test. On questions about the input or about knowledge (FPB, BoolQ, MMLU-Pro), GEPA beat the constant or found no clear gain over thinking off; on questions that ask for a prediction (14B mortality, descriptive; Autocast, exploratory), the harness ended near the constant and gave one label almost throughout while its gain over thinking off looked large. The constant label told the two apart wherever the gain was large. This rests on few tasks that also differ in label skew, number of labels and task type, so it is not shown to depend on the kind of question. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Are We Really Benchmarking Forecasting Models? The Impact of Preprocessing on Time Series Performance
docs.text:
Are We Really Benchmarking Forecasting Models? The Impact of Preprocessing on Time Series Performance Are We Really Benchmarking Forecasting Models? The Impact of Preprocessing on Time Series Performance arXiv:2610.09096v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: While established literature underscores the pivotal role of preprocessing in forecasting accuracy, this stage remains largely overlooked in current research. Modern benchmarks typically resort to simple scaling, failing to account for critical transformations required to address nonstationarity, such as differencing. This omission creates a significant structural preprocessing bias that favors models with built-in data treatments while obscuring the true potential of simpler architectures. We study this effect through a preprocessing-aware benchmark that evaluates 11 forecasting models across 16 reversible preprocessing pipelines on 29,000 M4 time series. Our results identify preprocessing as a key driver of forecasting performance. Optimizing preprocessing per series yields gains of approximately 27\% to 87\% across all evaluated models, with architectures lacking internalized preprocessing experiencing the most substantial improvements. This allows simpler architectures to become highly competitive with complex, state-of-the-art models in modern forecasting benchmarks. All resources and experimental results from this benchmark are stored in a comprehensive metadataset to support future metalearning tasks. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: 4-Tensor Attention Model for Semantic Physical Reality
docs.text:
4-Tensor Attention Model for Semantic Physical Reality 4-Tensor Attention Model for Semantic Physical Reality arXiv:2610.11716v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We describe a 4-tensor attention model that predicts the next semantic state of a scene, for video generation and robot planning. A window of states has positions (x, t) and two fibers, a semantic fiber and a temporal-context fiber, and one softmax normalizes attention jointly over the window. Frames and an agent's situation are written as those states; the encoder, the renderer, and the planner remain outside the update. To test the update on its own, we train on ROCStories, where each window poses the same next-sentence task at the semantic layer. On the validation split, with one seed per setting, the last-sentence cross-entropy on the three matched settings is lower for the 4-tensor model than for a free-running one-dimensional transformer by 5.3% at H=2, L=2, by 2.6% at H=4, L=2, and by 2.4% at H=4, L=3. At H=4, L=2 the parameter counts are nearly the same, 172.5M and 175.9M. On the same two GPUs that 4-tensor run finished in 2.4 hours and the baseline run in 45.2 hours; the baseline is trained by free-running decoding, one sequential forward pass per target token. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings
docs.text:
TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings TILE: Bridging LLMs and Table Foundation Models for Tabular Learning with Strings arXiv:2610.17065v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Real-world tables are often heterogeneous, combining numerical features with free-form string columns. Table foundation models (TFMs) excel on numerical tables but require strings to be encoded numerically, while large language models (LLMs) hold semantic knowledge but are not designed for tabular predictions. Most existing bridges use LLMs as plug-in encoders for cell strings, yet how to extract representations effectively for tabular learning remains underexplored. We show that the interface between LLMs and tables matters as much as the LLM itself. Applied cell-wise, larger LLMs do not give better features. With our interface, the same LLMs improve steadily with size. TILE (Table-Interfaced LLM Embeddings) combines four ingredients: row serialization to provide cross-column context, intermediate-layer extraction to avoid layers specialized for next-token prediction, columnar pooling to remove mean pooling's length bias, and by-pass features to route numbers and categories past the LLM. Paired with TFMs, TILE sets a new state of the art for tables with strings. Across 100 datasets, it beats the strongest baseline on $90\%$ of splits, with gains across 7 LLMs and 10 tabular learners, and ranks first on STRABLE's 108 datasets. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: CodeLift: Your Test Suite Is Secretly a Dense SWE Curriculum
docs.text:
CodeLift: Your Test Suite Is Secretly a Dense SWE Curriculum CodeLift: Your Test Suite Is Secretly a Dense SWE Curriculum arXiv:2610.17224v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The pass-all-test binary reward has become a standard recipe for training software engineering agents, but its sparsity eliminates difference of partially correct patches. The test pass-rate is a natural alternative. However, we find that it is not a reliable indicator of patch quality. A functionality being tested can be covered by either one challenging test or one hundred trivial tests, where the majority might be already satisfied pass-to-pass tests. We introduce CodeLift, a reinforcement learning method that dynamically calibrates pass-rate rewards, turning the test suite into an adaptive curriculum. At each iteration, CodeLift groups tests that kill the same patches and patches that pass the same tests, then gives more weight to test groups that fewer patch groups pass. This reduces the impact of majority simple tests and focuses more on what is still challenging. Within each rollout, CodeLift applies the same scoring rule to repository snapshots, assigning credit to useful actions even when later ones introduce regressions. Experiments on SWE benchmarks show that CodeLift consistently improves pass@1/2/4/8 over binary and pass-rate baselines. Analyses show that CodeLift provides dense, stable learning signals and unlocks the inherent curriculum in the test suite. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Transport What Shares the Conduction Pathway: Normal-Anchored SPD Geometric Transport for Source-Free Patient Adaptation of Holter and Patch ECG
docs.text:
Transport What Shares the Conduction Pathway: Normal-Anchored SPD Geometric Transport for Source-Free Patient Adaptation of Holter and Patch ECG Transport What Shares the Conduction Pathway: Normal-Anchored SPD Geometric Transport for Source-Free Patient Adaptation of Holter and Patch ECG arXiv:2610.24430v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Continuous electrocardiogram (ECG) streams are dominated by normal beats (87.9-98.6% of the label-free adaptation prefix in our four databases), and patient-specific waveform distortion is not shared by every beat class; under this combination, source-free and test-time adaptation methods that assume class-balanced target batches collapse. We propose Normal-Anchored Geometric Transport (NAGT, GA_NS), which estimates a closed-form symmetric positive-definite congruence map from label-free normal anchors in the first 5 min of each recording and applies it only to the normal and supraventricular prototypes, keeping the ventricular and fusion prototypes fixed. Decision rules were set on MIT-BIH and the rate-invariant RR head was adopted after the development databases (INCART, SVDB) had been opened; the frozen model was then evaluated once under a pre-specified locked evaluation protocol on the held-out Icentia11k chest-patch cohort. In 493 patients (973 recordings, 3,615,388 evaluated beats), NAGT raised the arrhythmia macro-F1 J from 34.5% to 48.7% ($\Delta J$ = +14.1 [+8.6, +19.3] pp; non-AF 43.9% to 59.8%) and outperformed all five Holm-adjusted comparators, including AdaBN, Tent and T3A. In post hoc analyses of the frozen outputs, ventricular false alarms fell by 68% (41.1 to 13.2 per hour) and 98.3% of normal beats stayed outside the alarm classes. Adaptation takes 5.8 ms per record without back-propagation. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Estimating Performance for Safe Deployment of Machine Learning Models
docs.text:
Estimating Performance for Safe Deployment of Machine Learning Models Estimating Performance for Safe Deployment of Machine Learning Models arXiv:2610.29262v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The main challenge in applying deep neural networks to real-world scenarios lies in distributional discrepancies between training and test datasets, often caused by variations in data acquisition conditions. Assessing the performance of pre-trained models without labels is crucial for safety, but this is complicated by deep models' overly optimistic probabilistic outputs, often exacerbated by class imbalances, leading to unreliable predictions. To address these issues, we introduce MOVAL, a novel MOdel eVALuation tool that estimates performance using unlabeled test data. MOVAL incorporates class-wise confidence calibration to adjust model outputs, allowing for the estimation of metrics beyond accuracy and mitigating the detrimental effects of class imbalance on confidence calibration. Additionally, we propose an ensemble approach that combines multiple calibrated confidence scores for a more robust solution. We validate MOVAL on natural and medical image datasets with various acquisition shifts, covering tasks from classification to segmentation. It achieves state-of-the-art results across evaluation metrics such as accuracy, F1-Score, AUC, and more. Furthermore, we demonstrate that MOVAL provides accurate performance estimations at the class, instance, and pixel levels, ensuring the transparent and safe deployment of machine learning models. We provide MOVAL as a deployment tool for monitoring and estimating performance under a range of domain shifts. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference?
docs.text:
When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference? When Does Dynamics Randomization Test Context Inference? arXiv:2610.32414v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Environments with randomized dynamics are widely used to ask whether world models need explicit context inference. However, randomization can leave little predictive information for a context encoder to add, because distinct latent parameters may produce similar transitions at visited states, or those states may already reveal the active context. We formalize the remaining one-step information as predictive headroom and compare kernels under fixed and visited state--action distributions to distinguish changes in query coverage from changes in context weights. We analyze discrete and continuous environments and find low headroom both when kernels differ little and when visitation reduces an otherwise large discrepancy. At the same time, resetting state components increases headroom, showing that context evidence accumulates in state. We propose reporting this headroom alongside the randomized parameters, so that gains from explicit context inference can be interpreted relative to the information missing from the current state and action. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters
docs.text:
Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters Satellite-derived bathymetry of Arabian Gulf ports under leakage-free validation: a multi-site benchmark of empirical, machine-learning and deep-learning models against 285,000 multibeam soundings, with an outlook for UAE waters arXiv:2610.33609v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Satellite-derived bathymetry (SDB) is often proposed as a low-cost complement to multibeam surveys of ports, but its accuracy is seldom measured on an area the model has never seen. We test SDB in the turbid, shallow and tidal waters of the Abu Dhabi coast against 285,619 multibeam soundings from twelve surveys at six port areas, reduced to Lowest Astronomical Tide. The Stumpf ratio, the Lyzenga transform, a monotonic gradient-boosted tree model (LightGBM) and a U-Net ensemble were trained on 72 Sentinel-2 images and tested in transfer to an unseen site and with local control (about 20% of a site's soundings, spatial blocks beyond a 225 m buffer). The validation design changed the result more than the model: the same LightGBM model gave 0.57 m RMSE under a random pixel split, 1.30 m under spatial blocks and 1.66 m at an unseen site. In transfer the Stumpf ratio (1.45 m) was not beaten by LightGBM, the U-Net or Lyzenga. With local control a hybrid of the tree output and the band ratio reached 1.11 m over 0-11 m, 67% of pixels within the IHO S-44 Order 2 tolerance and a conformal 95% interval with 95% observed coverage; in clear water it reached 0.29-0.53 m. The seabed could not be read beyond 11 m, and summer images were five to six times more turbid than winter ones. ICESat-2 ATL24 agreed with the surveys to 0.25 m after a depth-dependent offset was removed. A 60 m reconnaissance mosaic of 17,200 km2 of the UAE coast, calibrated cell by cell on ICESat-2 without any vessel survey, reached 1.42 m RMSE on held-out blocks over half of the product. Sentinel-2 SDB with about a hundred control depths per image is a usable reconnaissance and change-monitoring tool in these waters to about 10 m; it does not meet S-44 Order 1 without local control, and accuracies from random splits should not be taken as operational accuracy. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Hierarchical Cooperative GFlowNets
docs.text:
Hierarchical Cooperative GFlowNets Hierarchical Cooperative GFlowNets arXiv:2610.33968v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) are trained to sample objects from compositional spaces with probability proportional to a reward function, but ineffective exploration can cause learned samplers to concentrate on a few high-reward regions. An intuitive remedy is to train multiple GFlowNets independently in parallel and combine their samples. However, this does not prevent multiple models from collapsing onto the same high-reward areas, leaving large regions of the state space unexplored. With this in mind, we propose Hierarchical Cooperative GFlowNets (HCG), an approach that dynamically partitions the search space to coordinate discovery without relying on hand-crafted boundaries. HCG imposes an ordering in which the highest-ranked model may explore the entire space, while lower-ranked models are progressively pushed toward regions not covered by higher-ranked ones. We provide a theoretical characterization of how specific learning objectives can shift probability mass away from designated areas, instantiating this mechanism within our architecture. A shared classifier coordinates the hierarchy by partitioning the search space, keeping the GFlowNets independently parameterized and enabling asynchronous training. Furthermore, we derive a normalizer-weighted aggregation rule for the ensemble and prove that it recovers the target reward-proportional distribution under the stated assumptions. Finally, experiments across multimodal distributions, sequence generation, combinatorial optimization, and biological sequence design show that HCG improves mode coverage and target approximation, translating increases in the number of coordinated samplers into broader, complementary exploration. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Cumulative Marginal Matching for One-Step Diffusion
docs.text:
Cumulative Marginal Matching for One-Step Diffusion Cumulative Marginal Matching for One-Step Diffusion arXiv:2610.34575v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The sampling procedures of diffusion and flow-matching models involve hundreds of denoising steps incurring substantial inference time, which has motivated a growing body of work on training schemes for few-step and one-step generation. Existing approaches primarily seek to align the generation trajectory of few-step and base models, yet their training objectives only involve discrepancies at a single point in the trajectory, encouraging only local \emph{point-level} alignment. While recent methods such as \emph{Shortcut-CSL} introduce cumulative objective that enforce alignment over the entire trajectory, this is suboptimal as they do not directly enforce alignment between the distributions induced by the two models throughout the generation process. We propose \emph{Cumulative Marginal Matching} (CMM), a principled objective for few-step generation: by viewing flow-matching as a sequence of intermediate marginal distributions connecting the prior and data distributions, CMM directly optimizes the cumulative discrepancy between the base and few-step marginal distributions over the entire sequence. Specifically, we formulate this discrepancy using the Wasserstein-2 distance. By exploiting the pushforward representation of flow-matching, we transform an intractable cumulative Wasserstein objective into a tractable surrogate that can be optimized using samples from the intermediate marginal, which are readily generated through the conditional interpolation process of flow-matching. Furthermore, we show that the existing \emph{Shortcut-CSL} objective arises as a first-order approximation of that of the CMM, establishing a theoretical connection between the two objectives. Experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate improvement in generation quality over \emph{Shortcut-CSL} and other state-of-the-art one- and few-step baselines under identical training budgets. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
docs.text:
h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving arXiv:2610.35962v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: While progress in informal mathematics has come largely from scaling the chain-of-thought and agentic reasoning of frontier language models, formal theorem proving has increasingly relied on human-designed workflows around these models, such as planning, decomposition, and orchestrating specialized provers. This raises a bitter-lesson question: can a simple agentic loop that scales test-time compute match these workflows? The answer matters as formal verification must scale to keep up with frontier models producing research mathematics, yet new workflows rarely settle it, as their gains are often confounded with stronger models or more compute. We study this question with h1, a simple harness that gives a model an efficient interface to Lean 4 and keeps it working through verifier feedback and self-reflection, without imposing a decomposition or search structure. h1 reaches state-of-the-art results on PutnamBench, FATE-X, and FormalConjectures100-Solved, settles eight open problems in FormalConjectures, and, at matched models, matches or outperforms specialized workflows such as Goedel-Architect and AlphaProof Nexus, surprisingly showing that a single attempt (pass@1) can often scale to solve open problems. Through ablations and matched-model comparisons with Claude Code and AxProverBase, we find that simplicity alone is not enough: an efficient Lean interface largely determines cost and solve rate. We thus recommend that future work evaluate frontier models with efficient execution feedback before prescribing workflows, at the risk of bitter lessons. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning
docs.text:
When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning arXiv:2610.37239v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Multi-relational graph detectors learn from clean data how much to trust each relation, but an adversary pays a different price to manipulate each relation and each action; taking such costs as given, we ask when using a relation is worse than ignoring it. Our first main result proves that degree gating strictly beats every selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and that this window is sharp; on real graphs, validated gating gains exactly on the relations that meet these conditions and nowhere else. Our second shows that a per-node exposure bound, which extends to message passing, tells a platform which relation to harden: exposure per unit cost, computed without any attack, picks the relation whose hardening raises the exact trap threshold most in 15 of 16 cases, against at most 7 for informativeness, cheapness, or an analysis with equal edit costs. Supporting tools give exact worst cases for linear relational models, certified brackets for R-GCN and tree ensembles, and a finite-sample guarantee for adversarial validation, under which clean-trained graph detectors fall below their graph-free counterparts in 58 of 90 settings on six graphs. A selection protocol built on these results is never significantly worse than ignoring the graph; with at most four relations it mostly abstains, as validation alone would, and its cost-aware proposals help when relations are many, so far shown on synthetic graphs. Without cost information, the safe choice is to abstain. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection
docs.text:
Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection Normative Deviation Modeling for EEG-based Depression Detection arXiv:2610.37338v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Web-enabled digital health services are expanding access to physiological monitoring and mental health screening. However, electroencephalography (EEG)-based major depressive disorder (MDD) detection remains challenging across heterogeneous data sources, where individual variability and acquisition differences may affect disease-related representations. In this work, we investigate the use of healthy normative references for EEG-based MDD detection. Specifically, structural and distributional reference models are independently trained using healthy control (HC) recordings to characterize departures from healthy EEG patterns. We develop two diagnostic approaches that incorporate normative deviations at different representation levels. Scalar-level Normative Deviation-guided Diagnosis (S-NDD) summarizes structural and distributional deviations into scalar scores and integrates them with deep EEG representations. Feature-level Normative Deviation-guided Diagnosis (F-NDD) retains dimension-wise residuals and combines them with deep EEG representations through attention-based aggregation and auxiliary supervision. We also employ target HC-assisted score calibration for cross-source evaluation without updating the trained models. Experiments on two public EEG datasets examine both approaches under subject-independent within-source and bidirectional cross-source settings. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of normative deviation-guided diagnosis across different evaluation settings. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
docs.text:
Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness arXiv:2610.37657v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Foundation Model for the Human Gut Microbiome
docs.text:
TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Foundation Model for the Human Gut Microbiome TaxoMFM: A Taxonomy-Aware Foundation Model for the Human Gut Microbiome arXiv:2610.39316v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Existing gut microbiome foundation models typically use flat taxon representations, limiting their ability to exploit known taxonomic hierarchies. We introduce TaxoMFM, a microbiome foundation model that integrates taxonomic structure into self-supervised learning. TaxoMFM jointly learns abundance patterns across taxonomic ranks and relative proportions within groups through taxonomy-aware encoding and hierarchical compositional reconstruction. We further construct TaxoGut-HPP, comprising 100,806 gut microbiome profiles from 231 source cohorts and covering 40 classification and 8 regression tasks. TaxoMFM achieves competitive performance across disease, gut health, host trait, and liver ultrasound phenotype prediction. In cross-cohort zero-shot transfer, where target cohorts are excluded from both pretraining and downstream adaptation, TaxoMFM achieves AUROCs of 0.838, 0.736, and 0.722 for colorectal cancer, type 2 diabetes, and inflammatory bowel disease, respectively. Further analyses show that TaxoMFM recovers community changes across taxonomic scales, while preserving community information and producing consistent representations under database updates and species-vocabulary shifts. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/TaxoMFM-F16D/. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Turing LLM Post-Training: Calibrated Distillation and Efficient Dynamic-MoE Execution
docs.text:
Turing LLM Post-Training: Calibrated Distillation and Efficient Dynamic-MoE Execution Turing LLM Post-Training: Calibrated Distillation and Efficient Dynamic-MoE Execution arXiv:2610.39876v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study post-training for dynamically routed mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, focusing on integrating independently optimized specialists while keeping consolidation efficient. Our approach combines calibrated multi-teacher on-policy distillation (C-MOPD), which matches each selected teacher on a local Top-$K$ support with teacher-wise loss normalization and clipping, with an execution path that uses post-capacity bounded-width dispatch, final-route replay, and asynchronous rollout--training overlap. On Turing-20B-A2B, the selected model achieves a four-domain normalized integration score of 0.9988 and retains at least 90.16\% of the measured specialist gain in every domain. At matched $K=32$, the full calibration objective scores 0.9962, compared with 0.9724 without calibration and 0.9834 without clipping. At a matched 8K response cap, the model exceeds both shared SFT and Qwen3-8B on all four reasoning-enabled mathematics and code benchmarks (unweighted mean: 85.92, versus 80.33 for Qwen3-8B and 74.21 for SFT), and improves over SFT on ten of twelve broader evaluation metrics. In a PPU-based profile, the combined execution configuration reduces consolidation step time from 398.7 to 139.3 seconds, an observed 2.86$\times$ speedup over serial execution. These results demonstrate strong specialist integration alongside more efficient consolidation, while reflecting the complete training and execution framework rather than any single component. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: NECA: Neighbor Event Curve Augmentation for Multi-Horizon ICU Deterioration Prediction
docs.text:
NECA: Neighbor Event Curve Augmentation for Multi-Horizon ICU Deterioration Prediction NECA: Neighbor Event Curve Augmentation for Multi-Horizon ICU Deterioration Prediction arXiv:2610.40420v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Early prediction of ICU organ dysfunction events supports timely clinical monitoring and intervention, but estimating short-term organ-specific risk from early ICU records remains challenging due to irregular measurements, heterogeneous clinical variables, and the need to predict risk across multiple future horizons. Existing supervised models usually treat each patient as an isolated sample and do not explicitly use the observed event timing of similar historical patients. We propose Neighbor Event-Curve Augmentation (NECA), a model-agnostic method that retrieves training-set patients with similar early-window profiles and converts their subsequent organ dysfunction event onset times into cumulative event-curve features over 6h, 12h, 24h, and 42h. These features are concatenated with the original patient representation and used by standard downstream predictors. On PhysioNet 2012 and a 4,000-stay MIMIC-IV subset, NECA improves average PR-AUC and ROC-AUC across four organ dysfunction event tasks and seven supervised learners. The largest gain appears for neurological dysfunction events, where task-level average PR-AUC increases from 0.461 to 0.557 on PhysioNet 2012. Ablations show that clinically meaningful retrieval and horizon-specific neighbor risk drive most of the improvement, while the full cumulative curve adds task-dependent temporal context. These results support similar-patient event timing as a structured temporal risk signal for ICU organ dysfunction event prediction. The source code will be publicly released upon acceptance of this paper. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Discovering contemporaneous and lagged causal relations in autocorrelated nonlinear time series datasets
docs.text:
Discovering contemporaneous and lagged causal relations in autocorrelated nonlinear time series datasets Discovering contemporaneous and lagged causal relations in autocorrelated nonlinear time series datasets arXiv:2003.03685v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: The paper introduces a novel conditional independence (CI) based method for linear and nonlinear, lagged and contemporaneous causal discovery from observational time series in the causally sufficient case. Existing CI-based methods such as the PC algorithm and also common methods from other frameworks suffer from low recall and partially inflated false positives for strong autocorrelation which is an ubiquitous challenge in time series. The novel method, PCMCI$^+$, extends PCMCI [Runge et al., 2019b] to include discovery of contemporaneous links. PCMCI$^+$ improves the reliability of CI tests by optimizing the choice of conditioning sets and even benefits from autocorrelation. The method is order-independent and consistent in the oracle case. A broad range of numerical experiments demonstrates that PCMCI$^+$ has higher adjacency detection power and especially more contemporaneous orientation recall compared to other methods while better controlling false positives. Optimized conditioning sets also lead to much shorter runtimes than the PC algorithm. PCMCI$^+$ can be of considerable use in many real world application scenarios where often time resolutions are too coarse to resolve time delays and strong autocorrelation is present. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications
docs.text:
Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications Transport-Free Lower Bounds for Ollivier--Ricci Curvature in Higher-Order Networks: Scope, Tightness, and Computational Applications arXiv:2405.13302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study how the Bauer--Jost--Liu curvature bound applies to hypergraph Ollivier--Ricci curvature (ORC) and how its accuracy depends on local mass and geometry. An explicit weighted-graph representation shows how the graph theorem applies. A transport construction transfers the bounds to monotone pairwise hyperedge aggregations. We analyze endpoint cancellation under laziness, quantify the exact improvement over the earlier mixture bound, and characterize the extremal geometry at fixed endpoint and overlap statistics. Further results quantify worst-case slack, stability, and exactness on isolated hyperedges. A capacity-constrained short-detour refinement uses additional geometric information and improves monotonically as the query budget increases. As a computational application, a threshold cascade preserves exact transport decisions. Numerical verification and public-hypergraph experiments examine tightness, walk dependence, and aggregation, including evaluations on 42,940 finite pairwise comparisons and 64,620 public-data instances. Together, the results specify the scope, equality mechanisms, and computational uses of BJL-type hypergraph bounds. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks
docs.text:
Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks Learning Maximal Regions of Attraction on Compact Sets using Taylor Lyapunov Networks arXiv:2408.17246v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We consider the problem of learning maximal Lyapunov functions to compute the maximal region of attraction of nonlinear dynamical systems using neural networks. Two obstacles limit existing neural-network approaches: 1) finite-width approximations can fail to preserve the strict Lyapunov inequalities near the equilibrium, where they become arbitrarily weak, and 2) training is necessarily performed on a bounded computational domain for which the classical Lyapunov and Zubov theorems do not directly apply. To address these issues, first we derive Lyapunov and Zubov theorems directly on a prescribed compact computational domain, characterizing the maximal region of attraction within that domain as the solution of a boundary-value PDE. Second, we introduce the Taylor Lyapunov network, an architecture that prescribes the quadratic leading-order term via the system's linearization and represents the higher-order remainder through a structured cubic factorization, guaranteeing that any network in this class is a valid local Lyapunov function by construction. Finally, we prove that Taylor Lyapunov networks are universal approximators of maximal Lyapunov functions on compact domains, and combine these results into an unsupervised, physics-informed training procedure. Numerical experiments on systems of varying dimensions and stability types show that the proposed architecture is efficient at estimating the maximum region of attraction. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Time Will Tell: Harness Time to Denoise Collaborative Filtering
docs.text:
Time Will Tell: Harness Time to Denoise Collaborative Filtering Time Will Tell: Harness Time to Denoise Collaborative Filtering arXiv:2411.09181v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Neural graph collaborative filtering is a powerful tool for recommendation due to its superb capability of capturing the user-item interaction. Despite the substantial progress, the noisy nature of interaction data remains a significant challenge in collaborative filtering, especially for data collected from implicit feedback. Both noisy interactions and interactions crafted by malicious users could greatly degenerate model performance. To purify the input data and enhance model robustness, it is vital to understand how noisy interactions can be identified and rectified. Existing denoising methods focus on mining the correlation between user/item embeddings and noisy interactions, neglecting the temporal dimension for denoising. However, time information bears its natural and unique advantage in revealing noisy edges as we observe in this paper. In this work, we introduce a simple yet effective mechanism for generating time-aware user/item embeddings that capture both global preferences and temporal patterns. Two strategies, reweighting adjacency matrix (Tint-A) and reweighting loss function (Tint-L), are proposed to leverage the embeddings for the task of using \underline{t}ime \underline{in}forma\underline{t}ion to denoise \underline{c}ollaborative \underline{f}iltering (TintCF). Extensive experiments have been conducted on four real-world datasets to demonstrate the efficacy of our methods and illustrate how time information indeed helps identify and rectify noisy edges. Our codes are available at \href{https://github.com/xinyuu-he/TintCF}{https://github.com/xinyuu-he/TintCF}. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Lattice-Based Pruning of Recurrent Neural Networks via Poset Modeling: A Corrected Theory and a Matched-Sparsity Evaluation
docs.text:
Lattice-Based Pruning of Recurrent Neural Networks via Poset Modeling: A Corrected Theory and a Matched-Sparsity Evaluation Lattice-Based Pruning of Recurrent Neural Networks via Poset Modeling: A Corrected Theory and a Matched-Sparsity Evaluation arXiv:2502.16525v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Magnitude pruning of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) ignores how information flows between neurons. An earlier version proposed to model RNN dependencies as a partially ordered set (poset) and to retain the meet-irreducible elements of its dependency lattice. By Birkhoff's representation theorem, the meet-irreducible ideals of a finite poset are in bijection with its elements, so retaining them retains everything; the critical-set criterion used earlier selects precisely the elements comparable to all others, of which a dense recurrent layer has none. Condensing a thresholded dependency graph into strongly connected components yields a well-defined dependency order, a graded order score and an acyclic pruning rule; for Cohen-Grossberg networks and LSTMs, acyclic pruning makes local stability decompose over modules. For a 128-unit LSTM pruned at matched sparsity on row-wise and chunked sequential MNIST (three seeds, equal training budgets), the original rules remove every recurrent weight or equal random column pruning; the order score is no better than degree, PageRank or norm; trained weights show little directional bias; and imposing acyclicity from initialisation costs 2.1 and 10.5 percentage points at 50% and 90% sparsity. In the networks studied, order structure must be imposed rather than discovered. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: VisualSphinx: Large-Scale Synthetic Vision Logic Puzzles for RL
docs.text:
VisualSphinx: Large-Scale Synthetic Vision Logic Puzzles for RL VisualSphinx: Large-Scale Synthetic Vision Logic Puzzles for RL arXiv:2505.23977v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) are expected to perform effective multimodal reasoning and make logically coherent decisions, which is critical to tasks such as diagram understanding and spatial problem solving. However, current VLM reasoning lacks large-scale and well-structured training datasets. To bridge this gap, we propose VisualSphinx, a first-of-its-kind large-scale synthetic visual logical reasoning training dataset. To tackle the challenge of image synthesis with grounded answers, we propose a rule-to-image synthesis pipeline that extracts and expands puzzle rules from seed questions and generates executable rendering programs for puzzle assembly. Using standard GRPO with binary correctness rewards as a validation recipe, experiments show that VLMs trained on VisualSphinx benefit from the logical coherence and readability of our dataset and exhibit improved performance on logical reasoning tasks. The enhanced reasoning capabilities developed from VisualSphinx also benefit other reasoning tasks such as algebraic reasoning, arithmetic reasoning and geometry reasoning. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Critically-Damped Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics for Generative Modeling
docs.text:
Critically-Damped Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics for Generative Modeling Critically-Damped Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics for Generative Modeling arXiv:2506.21741v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) represent an entirely new class of generative AI methods that have yet to be fully explored. They use Langevin dynamics, represented as stochastic differential equations, to describe a process that transforms data into noise, the forward process, and a process that transforms noise into generated data, the reverse process. Many of these methods utilize auxiliary variables that formulate the data as a ``position" variable, and the auxiliary variables are referred to as ``velocity", ``acceleration", etc. In this sense, it is possible to ``critically damp" the dynamics. Critical damping has been successfully introduced in Critically-Damped Langevin Dynamics (CLD) and Critically-Damped Third-Order Langevin Dynamics (TOLD++), but has not yet been applied to dynamics of arbitrary order. The proposed methodology generalizes Higher-Order Langevin Dynamics (HOLD), a recent state-of-the-art diffusion method, by introducing the concept of critical damping from systems analysis. Similarly to TOLD++, this work proposes an optimal set of hyperparameters in the $n$-dimensional case, where HOLD leaves these to be user defined. Additionally, this work provides closed-form solutions for the mean and covariance of the forward process that greatly simplify its implementation. Experiments are performed on the CIFAR-10 and CelebA-HQ $256 \times 256$ datasets, and validated against the FID metric. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Distributed Information Bottleneck Theory for Multi-Modal Task-Aware Semantic Communication
docs.text:
Distributed Information Bottleneck Theory for Multi-Modal Task-Aware Semantic Communication Distributed Information Bottleneck Theory for Multi-Modal Task-Aware Semantic Communication arXiv:2510.04000v4 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Semantic communication shifts the focus from bit-level accuracy to task-relevant semantic delivery, enabling efficient and intelligent communication for next-generation networks. However, existing multi-modal solutions often process all available data modalities indiscriminately, ignoring that their contributions to downstream tasks are often unequal. This not only leads to severe resource inefficiency but also degrades task inference performance due to irrelevant or redundant information. To tackle this issue, we propose a novel task-aware distributed information bottleneck (TADIB) framework, which quantifies the contribution of any set of modalities to given tasks. Based on this theoretical framework, we design a practical coding scheme that intelligently selects and compresses only the most task-relevant modalities at the transmitter. To find the optimal selection and the codecs in the network, we adopt the probabilistic relaxation of discrete selection, enabling distributed encoders to make coordinated decisions with score function estimation and common randomness. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that our solution matches or surpasses the inference quality of full-modal baselines while significantly reducing communication and computational costs. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: DNNs, Dataset Statistics, and Correlation Functions
docs.text:
DNNs, Dataset Statistics, and Correlation Functions DNNs, Dataset Statistics, and Correlation Functions arXiv:2511.21715v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: This paper argues that dataset structure is important in image recognition tasks (among other tasks). Specifically, we focus on the nature and genesis of correlational structure in the actual datasets upon which DNNs are trained. We argue that DNNs are implementing a widespread methodology in condensed matter physics and materials science that focuses on mesoscale correlation structures that live between fundamental atomic/molecular scales and continuum scales. Specifically, we argue that DNNs that are successful in image classification must be discovering high order correlation functions. It is well-known that DNNs successfully generalize in apparent contravention of standard statistical learning theory. We consider the implications of our discussion for this puzzle. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: TIRx: A Unified Tile Primitive ML Compiler Across Heterogeneous Backends
docs.text:
TIRx: A Unified Tile Primitive ML Compiler Across Heterogeneous Backends TIRx: A Unified Tile Primitive ML Compiler Across Heterogeneous Backends arXiv:2601.19092v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Modern ML kernels evolve rapidly with new optimizations and hardware features. ML compiler abstractions must accommodate richer memory hierarchies, more forms of thread cooperation, and increasingly heterogeneous backends while retaining the control required for peak performance. We present TIRx, an ML compiler for GPUs and AI accelerators that exposes these ingredients through explicit interfaces. TIRx introduces an explicit execution-scope abstraction that captures participating hardware teams at multiple granularities. It also uses tensor layouts to map logical tensors to heterogeneous hardware spaces through named axes and shard/replica/offset semantics. Finally, it introduces tile-primitive dispatch, which lowers high-level operations to efficient implementations according to scope, layout, and backend. This design preserves native-level control while automating recurring address calculation, operand preparation, and instruction-loop generation. Our evaluation shows vendor-level performance across the latest GPUs and AI accelerators, while native-code case studies show substantial reductions in low-level implementation code. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Repair Brain Damage: Real-Numbered Error Correction Code for Neural Network
docs.text:
Repair Brain Damage: Real-Numbered Error Correction Code for Neural Network Repair Brain Damage: Real-Numbered Error Correction Code for Neural Network arXiv:2602.00076v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We study neural networks (NNs) operating under hardware-induced memory faults and computational errors, which can degrade reliability in safety-critical applications. To address this challenge, we propose a novel real-valued error correction coding (ECC) framework capable of detecting and correcting both types of errors. Our approach imposes structured real-valued linear constraints on network weights, enabling efficient error detection and recovery without increasing the number of parameters or compromising classification performance. The proposed method leverages linear programming and sparse recovery techniques to achieve low-complexity error correction. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first real-number-based ECC scheme that simultaneously addresses memory and computational errors in neural networks. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Parabolic Positional Encoding: A Vision-Centric, Principled, Extrapolatable, and General Approach
docs.text:
Parabolic Positional Encoding: A Vision-Centric, Principled, Extrapolatable, and General Approach Parabolic Positional Encoding: A Vision-Centric, Principled, Extrapolatable, and General Approach arXiv:2602.01418v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: We propose Parabolic Positional Encoding (PaPE), a parabola-based positional encoding for vision modalities in attention-based architectures. Given a set of vision tokens-such as from videos, event camera streams, images, or point clouds-our objective is to encode their positions while accounting for the characteristics of vision modalities. Prior works have largely extended positional encodings from 1D-sequences in language to nD-structures in vision, but only with partial account of vision characteristics. We address this gap by designing PaPE from principles distilled from prior work: translation invariance, rotation invariance (PaPE-RI), distance decay, directionality, and context awareness. Extrapolation experiments on ImageNet-1K show how PaPE extrapolates remarkably well, improving in absolute terms by up to 10.5 over the next-best encoding. Generality experiments on 8 datasets across 4 modalities show that PaPE is a general vision positional encoding, as PaPE matches the best baseline on 5 datasets and exceeds all on 2 datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/DTU-PAS/parabolic-position-encoding. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Expected Harm: Rethinking Safety Evaluation of (Mis)Aligned LLMs
docs.text:
Expected Harm: Rethinking Safety Evaluation of (Mis)Aligned LLMs Expected Harm: Rethinking Safety Evaluation of (Mis)Aligned LLMs arXiv:2602.01600v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Current evaluations of LLM safety predominantly rely on severity-based taxonomies to assess the harmfulness of models' responses to malicious queries. We argue that this formulation requires re-examination as it implicitly equates model output with realized harm while neglecting Execution Likelihood-the conditional probability of a threat being realized by a real-world actor given a model's response. In this work, we introduce Expected Harm, a metric that weights the severity of a jailbreak by its execution likelihood, modeled as a function of execution cost. Through empirical analysis of state-of-the-art models, we reveal a systematic Inverse Risk Calibration: models disproportionately exhibit stronger refusal behaviors for low-likelihood (high-cost) threats while remaining vulnerable to high-likelihood (low-cost) queries. Mechanistically, we first provide an analysis using linear probing, revealing that while refusal mechanisms linearly separate queries by severity, they do not use execution likelihood as an indicator for refusal. Then, we use Olmo-3's open-source staged checkpoints to trace the root cause of miscalibration to the Supervised Fine Tuning (SFT) training data distribution (82.8% of safety examples at cost levels 0-1) and show that cost representations are weak from the SFT stage onward. Finally, we demonstrate that this miscalibration creates a vulnerability: by exploiting this property, we increase the attack success rate of existing jailbreaks by up to $2\times$. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Cross-Fitted Clipped Covariance Estimation with a Data-Driven Tail-Energy Criterion
docs.text:
Cross-Fitted Clipped Covariance Estimation with a Data-Driven Tail-Energy Criterion Cross-Fitted Clipped Covariance Estimation with a Data-Driven Tail-Energy Criterion arXiv:2602.14020v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Heavy-tailed data make covariance estimation sensitive to the clipping level: stronger clipping reduces variance but increases bias. We study how to choose this clipping level from the data within a radial clipped covariance family. We propose the quantile tail-energy surrogate (QTES), a fully data-driven rule that combines a cross-fitted variance certificate with a held-out estimate of the tail energy removed by clipping. QTES requires no distributional prior parameters. For Euclidean clipping, the operator-norm bias is bounded by this scalar tail-energy quantity. Under a finite $L_4$ moment condition, together with a mild feasibility condition for the QTES block construction, we prove a uniform finite-sample calibration bound over a positive clipping grid and a finite-sample guarantee for the estimator selected by QTES, relative to the best candidate on that grid under the same variance-plus-bias criterion. Experiments on clean heavy-tailed and contaminated benchmarks show that QTES performs strongly across both regimes and remains competitive with the best reference methods considered. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Co-optimization for Adaptive Conformal Prediction
docs.text:
Co-optimization for Adaptive Conformal Prediction Co-optimization for Adaptive Conformal Prediction arXiv:2603.01719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: In regression, conformal prediction often suffers from inefficiency under heteroscedasticity and skewness due to fixed, non-adaptive interval centering. We propose CoCP, a new method that parameterizes prediction intervals by a center $m(x)$ and a radius $h(x)$, and alternates between learning $h(x)$ via smooth quantile regression on folded residuals and refining $m(x)$ using a smooth interval loss. This corrects mis-centering and drives the interval toward high-density regions. Beyond finite-sample marginal validity via split-conformal calibration, we prove that CoCP also attains asymptotic conditional coverage and optimal interval length if the base estimators are consistent. Experiments demonstrate that CoCP yields tighter intervals and achieves improved empirical conditional-coverage reliability. Code is available at https://github.com/jjoeysu/cocp. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: FlowTouch: View-Invariant Visuo-Tactile Prediction
docs.text:
FlowTouch: View-Invariant Visuo-Tactile Prediction FlowTouch: View-Invariant Visuo-Tactile Prediction arXiv:2603.08255v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Tactile sensation is essential for contact-rich manipulation tasks. It provides direct feedback on object geometry, surface properties, and interaction forces, enhancing perception and enabling fine-grained control. An inherent limitation of tactile sensors is that readings are available only when an object is touched. This precludes their use during planning and the initial execution phase of a task. Predicting tactile information from visual information can bridge this gap. A common approach is to learn a direct mapping from camera images to the output of vision-based tactile sensors. However, the resulting model will depend strongly on the specific setup and on how well the camera can capture the area where an object is touched. In this work, we introduce FlowTouch, a novel model for view-invariant visuo-tactile prediction. Our key idea is to use an object's local 3D mesh to encode rich information for predicting tactile patterns while abstracting away from scene-dependent details. FlowTouch integrates scene reconstruction and Flow Matching-based models for image generation. Our results show that FlowTouch is able to bridge the sim-to-real gap and generalize to new sensor instances. We further show that the resulting tactile images can be used for downstream grasp stability prediction. Our code, datasets and videos are available at https://flowtouch.github.io/ アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Proof-Carrying Materials: Falsifiable Safety Certificates for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
docs.text:
Proof-Carrying Materials: Falsifiable Safety Certificates for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials Proof-Carrying Materials: Falsifiable Safety Certificates for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials arXiv:2603.12183v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are deployed for high-throughput materials screening without formal reliability guarantees. We show that a single MLIP used as a stability filter misses 93% of density functional theory (DFT)-stable materials (recall 0.07) on a 25,000-material benchmark. Proof-Carrying Materials (PCM) closes this gap through three stages: adversarial falsification across compositional space, bootstrap envelope refinement with 95% confidence intervals, and Lean 4 formal certification. Auditing CHGNet, TensorNet and MACE reveals architecture-specific blind spots with near-zero pairwise error correlations (r <= 0.13; n = 5,000), confirmed by independent Quantum ESPRESSO validation (20/20 converged; median DFT/CHGNet force ratio 12x). A risk model trained on PCM-discovered features predicts failures on unseen materials (AUC-ROC = 0.938 +/- 0.004) and transfers across architectures (cross-MLIP AUC-ROC ~ 0.70; feature importance r = 0.877). In a thermoelectric screening case study, PCM-audited protocols discover 62 additional stable materials missed by single-MLIP screening - a 25% improvement in discovery yield. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: A Controlled Comparison of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting: Evidence from 918 Experiments
docs.text:
A Controlled Comparison of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting: Evidence from 918 Experiments A Controlled Comparison of Deep Learning Architectures for Multi-Horizon Financial Forecasting: Evidence from 918 Experiments arXiv:2603.16886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Reliable comparison of deep learning architectures for financial forecasting requires controlled evaluation that separates architectural effects from hyperparameter tuning, random initialization, forecast horizon, and asset characteristics. We present a five-stage benchmark using equal-budget Bayesian hyperparameter optimization, category-level configuration freezing, three-seed final training, held-out metric aggregation, and rank-based statistical validation. Nine architectures from Transformer, MLP/linear, convolutional, and recurrent families are evaluated with direct multi-step prediction from five OHLCV features across 12 assets (four cryptocurrency, four foreign exchange, four equity-index instruments), using chronological 70/15/15 splits of 30,000 hourly windows per asset at 4- and 24-hour horizons. The benchmark includes 918 runs (270 optimization trials, 648 final training runs). Across 24 asset-horizon points, ModernTCN has mean rank 1.333 and the lowest RMSE in 18 points (75.0%), followed by PatchTST (mean rank 2.000). Global ranking differences are strongly supported by an Iman-Davenport test (F(8,184)=101.36, p<1e-15), with 33 of 36 Holm-adjusted pairwise comparisons significant. Rankings are consistent across horizons for all 12 assets (rho>=0.683; Stouffer p=3.47e-10), while errors increase at the longer horizon. Architecture explains 99.90% of raw error variance and 68.33% after within-slot normalization excluding LSTM; seed variance contributes at most 0.04% (0.02% without LSTM). Mean directional accuracy is 50.08%. These findings provide a statistically validated comparison of nine architectures, identify ModernTCN and PatchTST as leading performers under the evaluated conditions, and offer a reproducible benchmark for multi-asset financial time-series forecasting. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: M$^\star$: Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness
docs.text:
M$^\star$: Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness M$^\star$: Every Task Deserves Its Own Memory Harness arXiv:2604.11811v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Large language model agents rely on a memory harness to write, organize, retrieve, and use past experience. A harness that works for one task often fails on another, because conversations, embodied planning, and expert reasoning require different storage and retrieval behavior. To address this limitation, we introduce Mstar, a method that automatically discovers task-optimized memory programs through reflective code evolution. Specifically, Mstar operationalizes a memory harness as an executable Python memory program that defines the Schema, Logic, and Instruction, and optimizes these components jointly. We evaluate Mstar on four tasks covering conversation, embodied planning, and specialized reasoning. Our results demonstrate that Mstar improves performance over existing baselines across all evaluated tasks. Furthermore, the evolved memory programs exhibit structurally distinct processing mechanisms for each evaluated domain. These findings suggest that every task benefits from its own memory harness, and that memory-program search provides a concrete way to discover it. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: AMMA: A Multi-Chiplet Memory-Centric Architecture for Low-Latency 1M Context Attention Serving
docs.text:
AMMA: A Multi-Chiplet Memory-Centric Architecture for Low-Latency 1M Context Attention Serving AMMA: A Multi-Chiplet Memory-Centric Architecture for Low-Latency 1M Context Attention Serving arXiv:2604.26103v3 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: All current LLM serving systems place the GPU at the center, from production-level attention-FFN disaggregation to NVIDIA's Rubin GPU-LPU heterogeneous platform. Even academic PIM/PNM proposals still treat the GPU as the central hub for cross-device communication. Yet the GPU's compute-rich architecture is fundamentally mismatched with the memory-bound nature of decode-phase attention, inflating serving latency while wasting power and die area on idle compute units. The problem is compounded as reasoning and agentic workloads push context lengths toward one million tokens, making attention latency the primary user-facing bottleneck.
